title: Sections at a pro-étale geometric point
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$,
and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring.

1. The functor $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},-)$ on sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules
   is exact; hence $R\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},M)$ is computed termwise for
   $M\in D^+(P_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.
2. For $L\in D^+(P_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the complex $L$ is (up to the equivalence
   between sheaves on $P_{\Et}$ and $\Lambda$-modules given by global
   sections) a complex of $\Lambda$-modules $L(P)$, and
   $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},\nu_P^*L)\simeq L(P)$ canonically.
3. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, $\bar y:P\to Y$ a geometric point,
   $a:X_{\bar y}\to P$ and $i:X_{\bar y}\to X$ the projections, and
   $K=\nu_X^*K_{\mathrm{ét}}$ with $K_{\mathrm{ét}}\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$
   having torsion cohomology. Then there are canonical isomorphisms

   $$
   (Rf_*K_{\mathrm{ét}})_{\bar y}\simeq\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},\bar y^*Rf_*K)
   \simeq R\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\mathrm{proét}},i^*K),
   $$

   and the composite agrees with the étale fibre isomorphism
   $(Rf_*K_{\mathrm{ét}})_{\bar y}\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\Et},i^{-1}K_{\mathrm{ét}})$
   followed by the comparison $R\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\Et},-)\to
   R\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\mathrm{proét}},\nu^*-)$.

proof.text: The ring $\Omega$ is w-contractible in the ring sense of [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Indeed $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a singleton, so its closed-point set is closed, every point has a unique closed specialization, and its component space is extremally disconnected (its only opens are the empty set and the singleton). Its only local ring is $\Omega$. The pair $(\Omega,0)$ is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: for every finite $\Omega$-algebra $B$, the map $B\to B/0B$ is the identity, so its idempotents lift uniquely. Its residue field is the separably closed field $\Omega$. Thus it is w-strictly local as well. This checks the hypotheses needed to evaluate at the affine weakly contractible terminal object $P$; it requires no assertion that all weakly etale algebras are ind-etale.

source.place: (1), verification of the weakly contractible point

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-wc-sections-exact] with $X=U=P$ and the constant sheaf of rings with value $\Lambda$. It says exactly that sections of module sheaves at this affine w-contractible object are exact. Apply [det-pe-wc-sections-derived] to the same object and ring: for any representing complex $M^\bullet$, its canonical comparison $M^\bullet(P)\to R\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},M)$ is an isomorphism. In particular the assertion holds for bounded-below $M$. This proves (1), with the natural termwise-to-derived comparison rather than an arbitrary choice of isomorphism.

source.place: (1), exact sections and their derived comparison

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], $\Gamma(P_{\Et},-)$ is an exact equivalence of module sheaves with $\Lambda$-modules, for this arbitrary ring $\Lambda$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections] to the affine scheme $P$ and its basis object $P$, presented by the constant one-object etale system $P$. It gives the natural module isomorphism $(\nu_P^*F)(P)=F(P)$ for every etale module sheaf $F$. The comparison inverse image is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]; this also gives module exactness because kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Exact functors act termwise on derived categories and preserve bounded-below objects by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Consequently the sheaf isomorphisms just obtained form an isomorphism of section complexes for any representative of $L$, descend through quasi-isomorphisms, and identify $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},\nu_P^*L)$ with $L(P)$. This proves (2).

source.place: (2), exact equivalence and comparison on the terminal affine

proof.text:
In (3) put $g=\bar y$, $f'=a$, and $g'=i$. The map $a$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Both $f$ and $a$ are qcqs: by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] they are quasi-compact; their diagonals are closed immersions, whose inverse images of affine opens are affine spectra of quotient rings by [def-weil-closed-immersion], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. This is quasi-separatedness by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. In the following formulas write $A_T=\nu_T^*$, $l_u=u_{\Et}^{-1}$, $r_u=Ru_{\Et,*}$, $p_u=u_{\mathrm{proét}}^*$, and $s_u=Ru_{\mathrm{proét},*}$. The pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives $\alpha_u:A_Ul_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_V$ for every $u:U\to V$. Use throughout the fixed derived comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-fixed-derived-comparisons], whose direct-image comparison is the derived underived restriction mate, not a separately chosen isomorphism. The arbitrary-ring statement [stage3-proetale-comparison-counit] supplies its counit identity and explicitly treats this fixed direct-image comparison as an isomorphism. For the qcqs maps just verified, [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] gives $\beta_u:A_Vr_u\xrightarrow{\sim}s_uA_U$ for $u=f,a$. Thus
$$S_L=p_g(\beta_{f,L})\circ\alpha_{g,r_fL}:A_Pl_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}p_gs_fA_XL.$$
Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] is natural in the abelian sheaf; applying this naturality to every scalar endomorphism makes the identification $\Lambda$-linear. Applied degreewise and then to complexes using its exact functors, it identifies the usual geometric stalk with $\Gamma(P_{\Et},l_gr_fK_{\mathrm{ét}})$. Step 3 and $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},S_{K_{\mathrm{ét}}})$ give the first isomorphism in (3). No finiteness assumption on $\Lambda$ was used.

source.place: (3), first comparison isomorphism and the qcqs hypotheses

proof.text: The bounded-below comparison [sk-prop-sf-comparison] supplies the derived unit hypothesis in [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence]. Therefore $K=A_XK_{\mathrm{ét}}$ belongs to $D^+_{\mathrm{class}}$. Its cohomology is torsion: exactness gives $H^q(K)=A_XH^q(K_{\mathrm{ét}})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. To check torsion directly, put $F=H^q(K_{\mathrm{ét}})$ and form its kernel subsheaves $F[n]$ as module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], their kernels and filtered colimit have the corresponding underlying abelian sheaves. Thus the torsion hypothesis says $F\cong\varinjlim_{n\geq1}F[n]$, indexed by the positive integers ordered by divisibility, using [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. The fixed-coefficient inverse-image adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] is obtained from the set adjunction by restricting to maps commuting with addition and scalar actions; naturality of its unit and counit ensures that adjuncts are linear. It is therefore an adjunction for this arbitrary $\Lambda$, so the inverse image preserves this colimit (maps from its image correspond to compatible maps from the stages). Forgetting again with [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], its exactness from Step 3 identifies $A_XF[n]$ with $(A_XF)[n]$. Thus their colimit is $A_XF$. Apply [sk-thm-properbasechange] to the cartesian square with $g=\bar y$: the specified pro-etale exchange $E^p_K:p_gs_fK\to s_ap_iK$ is an isomorphism. Applying the exact sections functor from Step 2 gives an isomorphism to $\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{proét}},Ra_*i^*K)$.

source.place: (3), classical torsion hypothesis and proper exchange

proof.text: For completeness the composition with derived global sections over the point has a direct resolution calculation. The inverse image $i^*$ is exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], hence preserves the cohomological lower bound by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Start with a complex $C$ representing $i^*K$ and a bound $n$ below which its cohomology vanishes. Replace it by the good truncation with zero terms below $n$, term $\operatorname{coker}(d^{n-1})$ in degree $n$, and terms $C^r$ above $n$ with induced differentials: the projection from $C$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at least $n$, and both sides have zero cohomology below $n$. This is a bounded-below representative. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] to obtain its bounded-below K-injective resolution $J$. The resolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] can use $J$: by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the isomorphism between $J$ and the fixed K-injective resolution is represented by a homotopy equivalence; the additive functor $a_*$ preserves its homotopy inverse. Therefore $Ra_*i^*K$ is represented by $a_*J$. Sections on $P$ are exact by Step 2, so their derived value on this representative is the ordinary complex $\Gamma(P,a_*J)$. The section formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives the equality of complexes $\Gamma(P,a_*J)=\Gamma(X_{\bar y},J)$, which computes $R\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\mathrm{proét}},i^*K)$. The equality commutes with morphisms of resolutions since it is equality of evaluations and restriction maps in every degree. Therefore it is the canonical derived-sections composition comparison, and proves the second isomorphism in (3).

source.place: (3), composition of sections, expanded on a single resolution

proof.text: Put $L=K_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and $T_L=s_a(\alpha_{i,L})\circ\beta_{a,l_iL}:A_Pr_al_iL\xrightarrow{\sim}s_ap_iA_XL$. Apply the generic coefficient-exchange statement [lem-weil-pbc-coefficient-exchange-mates] to the geometric-fibre square of Step 4, with source adjunctions $l_f\dashv r_f$ and $l_a\dashv r_a$ on $D^+$ of the etale sites, target adjunctions $p_f\dashv s_f$ and $p_a\dashv s_a$ on the pro-etale sites, horizontal functors $l_g,l_i$ and $p_g,p_i$, square transformations $\theta^e:l_al_g\to l_il_f$ and $\theta^p:p_ap_g\to p_ip_f$, vertical coefficient functors $A_Y,A_X,A_{Y'},A_{X'}$, pull comparisons $\alpha_f,\alpha_a$ (invertible) and $\alpha_g,\alpha_i$, push comparisons $\beta_f,\beta_a$, and exchange maps $E^e$ and $E^p$. Its hypotheses are checked as follows. The exchange counit equations $\varepsilon^e_{a,l_iL}\circ l_a(E^e_L)=l_i(\varepsilon^e_{f,L})\circ\theta^e_{r_fL}$, and the same for $E^p$, are the definition of both exchanges as unit-square-counit mates [sk-def-exchange] (the pro-etale one by [sk-thm-properbasechange], which defines it from $p_u,s_u$ in the same way). The push mate equations $\varepsilon^p_{u}\circ p_u(\beta_{u,M})=A(\varepsilon^e_{u,M})\circ\alpha_{u,r_uM}^{-1}$ for $u=f,a$ are [stage3-proetale-comparison-counit] precomposed with $\alpha_{u,r_uM}^{-1}$; it applies to the fixed comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-fixed-derived-comparisons], for arbitrary commutative $\Lambda$, since $f$ and $a$ are qcqs by Step 4. The pull-comparison cube $\theta^p_{A_YN}\circ p_a(\alpha_{g,N})\circ\alpha_{a,l_gN}=p_i(\alpha_{f,N})\circ\alpha_{i,l_fN}\circ A_{X'}(\theta^e_N)$ is [stage3-proetale-comparison-square] with $g'=i$, $f'=a$. The conclusion, at $L$, is $E^p_{A_XL}\circ p_g(\beta_{f,L})\circ\alpha_{g,r_fL}=s_a(\alpha_{i,L})\circ\beta_{a,l_iL}\circ A_P(E^e_L)$, that is $E^p_{A_XL}\circ S_L=T_L\circ A_P(E^e_L)$.

source.place: (3), last sentence: explicit counit and square calculation

proof.text: Choose a bounded below injective representative $I$ of $l_iL$ and a bounded below injective resolution $A_{X_{\bar y}}I\to J$, by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. Apply [lem-pbc-torsion-stalk-proetale-resolution-map] with $Z=X_{\bar y}$ and $F=l_iL$. It identifies the section map of the fixed $\beta_{a,l_iL}$ of [def-weil-pbc-fixed-derived-comparisons] with $\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\Et},I)\to\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\mathrm{proét}},A_{X_{\bar y}}I)\to\Gamma(X_{\bar y,\mathrm{proét}},J)$, the canonical fibre-cohomology comparison. Composing with $s_a(\alpha_i)$ identifies $\Gamma(P,T_L)$ with this comparison followed by the pullback identification $A_{X_{\bar y}}l_iL\simeq p_iA_XL$.

source.place: (3), agreement with the canonical etale fibre map and cohomology comparison

proof.text: For the etale section composition, the same $I$ computes $r_al_iL$ by $a_*I$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The point-section functor is exact [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], and degreewise $\Gamma(P,a_*I)=\Gamma(X_{\bar y},I)$. The etale fibre morphism is the etale exchange mate followed by this section composition, so under these identifications it is precisely $\Gamma(P_{\Et},E^e_L)$ [sk-def-exchange]. Apply point sections to the equality in Step 7 and use Steps 3, 6 and 8. It identifies the composite in (3) with the etale fibre morphism followed by the canonical fibre comparison. That comparison is an isomorphism by [sk-prop-sf-comparison]; hence the etale fibre morphism is an isomorphism too. This proves the last clause for arbitrary $\Lambda$.
